# Job Chapter 29 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 426v–427r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/JOB_029_page_001.jpg, JOB_029_page_002.jpg

---

**29:1** And-continued [vayosef] Iyyov to-take-up [se'et] his-discourse [meshalo] and-said:

**29:2** "Who would-give-me [mi yitteneni] as-[in] the-months of-old [qedem], as-[in] the-days God [Eloah] watched-over-me [yishmreni],

**29:3** when-he-caused-to-shine [be-hillo] his-lamp [nero] over my-head [roshi], by-his-light [le-oro] I-would-walk [elekh] [through] darkness [choshekh];

**29:4** as I-was in-the-days of-my-autumn [chorpi], when-the-counsel [sod] of-God [Eloah] [was] upon my-tent [ohali];

**29:5** when-yet the-Almighty [Shaddai] [was] with-me, around-me [sevivotai] [were] my-young-ones [ne'arai];

**29:6** when-my-steps [halichai] were-washed [birechots] in-curds [be-chem'ah], and-the-rock [tsur] poured-out [yatsuq] for-me streams of-oil [palgei shamen].

**29:7** When-I-went-out [be-tse'ti] [to] the-gate [sha'ar] upon [alei] the-city [qaret], in-the-square [ba-rechov] I-prepared [akhin] my-seat [moshavi] —

**29:8** the-young-men [ne'arim] saw-me [ra'uni] and-hid [nechba'u], and-the-aged [yeshishim] rose [qamu] and-stood [amadu].

**29:9** Princes [sarim] restrained [atsu] their-words [be-millim], and-a-hand [kaf] they-placed [yasimu] upon their-mouth [le-fihem].

**29:10** The-voice of-the-nobles [negidim] was-hidden [nechba'u], and-their-tongue [lshonam] clung [davqah] to-their-palate [le-chikkam].

**29:11** For the-ear [ozen] [that] heard [shame'ah] — it-called-me-blessed [te'ashireni]; and-the-eye [ayin] [that] saw [ra'atah] — it-bore-witness [vatta'ideni] for-me.

**29:12** For I-delivered [amallet] the-poor [ani] [who] cried-out [meshawe'a], and-the-fatherless [yatom] and-[him who had] no helper [ozer] for-him.

**29:13** The-blessing of-the-perishing [oved] came upon-me, and-the-heart [lev] of-the-widow [almanah] I-caused-to-sing [arnin].

**29:14** Righteousness [tsedeq] I-put-on [lavashti] and-it-clothed-me [vayilbasheni]; as-a-robe [ki-me'il] and-a-turban [tsanif] [was] my-justice [mishpati].

**29:15** Eyes [einayim] I-was to-the-blind [la-ivver], and-feet [raglayim] to-the-lame [la-pisseach] [was] I.

**29:16** A-father [av] I [was] to-the-needy [la-evyonim]; and-the-case [riv] [of him] I-did-not know [lo yadati] I-searched-out [echqerehu].

**29:17** And-I-broke [va'ashabberah] the-jaws [mattle'ot] of-the-unrighteous [avval], and-from-his-teeth [mi-shinnav] I-cast-out [ashlik] [the] prey [teref].

**29:18** And-I-said [va'omar], 'With my-nest [im qinni] I-shall-expire [egva], and-like-the-sand [ka-chol] I-shall-multiply [arbeh] [my] days.

**29:19** My-root [shorshi] [is] spread-out [patuach] to the-waters [elei mayim], and-dew [tal] will-lodge [yalin] upon my-branch [qetsiri].

**29:20** My-glory [kevodi] [is] fresh [chadash] with-me, and-my-bow [qashti] in-my-hand [be-yadi] is-renewed [tachalif].'

**29:21** To-me they-listened [shame'u] and-waited [veyichelu], and-they-were-silent [yidmu] for my-counsel [la'atsati].

**29:22** After my-word [davari] they-did-not speak-again [lo yishnu]; and-upon-them my-speech [millati] dropped [tittof].

**29:23** And-they-waited [veyichelu] for-me as-for-the-rain [ka-matar]; and-their-mouths [pihem] they-opened-wide [pa'aru] for-the-spring-rain [le-malqosh].

**29:24** I-laughed [eschaq] at-them — they-did-not believe [lo ya'aminu]; and-the-light of-my-face [or panai] they-did-not cast-down [lo yappilun].

**29:25** I-chose [evchar] their-way [darkam] and-sat [eshev] [as] chief [rosh]; and-I-dwelt [eshkon] as-a-king [ke-melekh] in-a-troop [ba-gedud], as-one-who-comforts [ke-asher] mourners [avelim yenachem]."

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.4 — "the days of my autumn":** Hebrew *chorpi* — "my autumn/harvest." Some read this as "my prime" or "my ripeness." The agricultural metaphor suggests a time of abundance and fruitfulness.

**v.6 — "the rock poured out streams of oil":** Hyperbolic imagery of abundance — olive trees growing on rocky hillsides produced oil so abundantly it seemed the rock itself was producing it.

**v.14 — "I put on righteousness and it clothed me":** The clothing metaphor makes justice not an external garb but a second skin. Job's righteousness was not performed — it was worn, lived, inhabited.

**v.18 — "like the sand" or "like the phoenix":** Hebrew *chol* can mean "sand" (long life) or "phoenix" (the mythical bird of rebirth). Both readings support Job's expectation of long life. EMET retains "sand" as the primary MT reading.

*— EMET*
